title: Home
text:
👋 Welcome to my portfolio for MUSA 5080: Public Policy Analytics at the University of Pennsylvania.
This site documents my work in the Master of Urban Spatial Analytics program — weekly notes, course assignments, and a final project applying data analysis to urban policy questions.



I’m a student in the MUSA program at Penn. My background is in computer science and data science. I have research experience in educational technologies and learning science. I have been working as a software engineer for the past 3 years. I’m interested in exploring the intersection of data and urban issues to create opportunities to expand information accessibility.




Weekly Notes — what I’m learning each week
Assignments — analyses completed for the course
About — more background and how to reach me






Email: ctrac@upenn.edu
GitHub: @cindytrac

title: Week 1: Getting Set Up
text:
Key Concepts
Three places a file can live:

My computer — where I edit
GitHub.com — where it’s stored
My live site — what the world sees

The loop: Edit → Save → Render → Commit → Push → Wait → Refresh
website = folder of html files (quarto) + computer that is always on (github)
Anatomy of a .qmd:

YAML (delineated by - - -)
Markdown .md (text written by you)
Code Chunks (delineated by ```)

title: Week 1: Getting Set Up
text:
Proving R Works
The chunk below runs when this page renders. If you can see a result underneath it on your published site, R and Quarto are talking to each other correctly.

sessionInfo()$R.version$version.string

[1] "R version 4.6.1 (2026-06-24)"


What happens after you render a page?

The file is read from top to bottom.
Finds code chunks.
Sends them to R, gets results back.
Gives text and results into HTML.

title: About Me
text:
📍 New England-born and previously NYC-based.
👩🏻‍💻 I studied computer science and data science at Worcester Polytechnic Institute. I was also trained as a high school technology/engineering teacher through WPI’s Teacher Preparation Program. I’ve worked as a software engineer for the past 3 years.
⭐️ My interest in information accessibility and care for community outreach has manifested in various ways. I did undergraduate research in learning science and educational technologies. I taught students technology, engineering, and computer science through programs like Girls Who Code and Engineering Ambassadors as well as in formal classrooms. I volunteer and am involved in outreach programs, both locally (HYPER) and nationally (MITES). I currently sit on the Alumni Advisory Council for Girls Who Code.
🗺️ Through MUSA, I hope to bridge the intersection of data, computer science, and urban policy to enable positive change in underserved communities by broadening access to data that impacts them.
